raised.claim: isLegalScope accepts a scope with non-empty beer_ids even when its where consists solely of a review_class term.
raised.why_it_breaks: model proposes new_issue with scope {beer_ids:[1], where:[{col:'review_class',op:'=',value:'matcher_bug'}]}; isLegalScope returns true so the issue is created; any future matcher_bug row satisfies the where term in rowSatisfiesScope and attaches, recreating the #347 dumping-ground behaviour the guard was written to prevent.

raised.claim: describeTerm prints the value (including null) for operators that have no value in the ScopeTermSchema (empty/non_empty/is_null etc.).
raised.why_it_breaks: AnalysisSchema.parse of a tool response produces {col:'brewery',op:'empty',value:null} (tool schema forces the property); renderScopeBlock calls describeTerm which yields 'brewery empty null'; the human Scope: line written into the issue body therefore contains literal null.

raised.claim: guardHits are only emitted in the verdict-shortfall warn when the number of model-provided verdicts is less than the batch size.
raised.why_it_breaks: model returns a verdict for every orphan, three of which reference an illegal-scope new_issue; covered === batch so the if is false, the warn (the line intended to surface guardHits) is never written, only the generic skipped count appears in the result line; a looping model emitting the same illegal proposal is not visible in one line.
